metadata.title: Ternary Network Floats: a datapath with no multiplier anywhere (record version)
metadata.notes: Record version: the manuscript entire, from which the shorter papers of the series are cut. The cut is a program (make-series.py), not a hand edit, so the shorter papers cannot silently diverge from this text. Three claims are withdrawn here rather than in an erratum: the throughput-per-area ranking, the no-survivors corollary at matched physical width, and the claim that TNF4 trains where nothing else does.
metadata.description:
Record version — the manuscript entire, cut nowhere. The shorter papers of this series are honest only if the material they defer to is obtainable; this is that material.

A ternary node has three sites that could carry a number format; one needs to. The weight is a code: multiplying by it is a sign-select. The sample arrives ADC-native. The accumulator alone has a range to spend, and Ternary Network Floats spend it — a sign, a balanced-ternary exponent of Et trits, an M-bit mantissa, 1 + Et + M = N.

Budget convention, stated once and binding throughout. 1 + Et + M = N counts the exponent as Et trit positions. It is a specification convention, not a storage claim, and this paper uses two budgets under two explicit names. The nominal budget is 1 + Et + M = N; the physical budget is 1 + ⌈Et log₂ 3⌉ + M ≤ N, which is what a packed binary word costs. The two differ by three cells at Et = 4 and seven at Et = 11, so the adopted 16-bit rung (Et, M) = (4, 11) occupies 19 physical bits. The canonical name of a rung is now its bit width: TNF4, TNF8, TNF16, TNF32 and TNF64 are 6, 10, 19, 36 and 69 bits. The nominal names are kept only as aliases, because 4, 8, 16, 32, 64 is exactly the IEEE width sequence and a row reading “TNF16 against binary16” looks matched and is not. Under the physical budget TNF holds no advantage at 16 or 32 bits, and no claim of the form “TNF wins at equal width” appears anywhere without its budget attached.

The weight is GFTernary, a two-bit {−φ, 0, +φ} alphabet, and it is where the multiplier is decided. Removing one rather than cheapening it requires the weight lattice to be closed under weight application and accumulation alike. ℤ[φ] is, because φ² = φ + 1: applying a weight is the Fibonacci step (a, b) → (b, a + b), accumulation is componentwise, and a layer’s linear path is exact. Machine-checked in Coq.

Closure does not single out φ; enumeration does. A scale is multiplier-free exactly when it is an algebraic integer whose companion matrix has entries in {0, ±1}. Degree two admits φ alone, and nothing lies between the shift and φ. The family rd = r + 1 reaches any granularity at one addition and d registers: fineness costs registers, not adders.

The throughput-per-area ranking is withdrawn. It read 0.1797 MHz/LUT for GFTernary against 0.1631 for the next entry, and it cannot stand: re-measurement found that on-die check logic had been folded to constants at synthesis in fourteen of twenty-eight clauses, so every area figure in that comparison measured a design with its checks deleted, and no honest (area, frequency) pair existed anywhere in the corpus. Taken again with both numbers from the same build, frequency follows Fmax = 4397 · LUT−0.648 (R² = 0.920) across a 39.6× span of area — which makes MHz per LUT a proxy for size rather than a figure of merit. Size explains 92% of frequency and structure the rest. What survives is an area result, which no re-measurement moved: on an XC7A200T the folded ternary neuron costs 28.0 LUT per weight at fan-in 8, rising to 33.1 and 33.2 at fan-in 16 and 32, with no DSP at any fan-in.

Which rung follows from the budget — φ at four bits, r⁵ = r³ + 1 at five, r⁶ = r + 1 at six — reaching 3.7% of fp32 at six bits and one adder. On the block axis the element is closed, the best eight-level codebook beating a deployed one by 0.9%, and the scale is not: a φ grid at four bits yielded lower perplexity than MXFP4 in the two evaluated models, at 0.125 fewer bits per weight.

Applicability is stated as a threshold and then tested against it. The scalar is D = mean(|log₂|x||); the threshold is a property of the rung, not of the family — D ≳ 9.5 at sixteen physical cells and D ≳ 21.9 at thirty-two, with a third rung admitting no threshold at all — and it is a conjunction with the range condition, which does most of the excluding. Eleven intermediate quantities of a real GPT-2 block satisfy none of it, because normalisation is what destroys the property. Seven of twenty-two candidate pairs outside neural inference do satisfy it, at 1.23× to 4.00×: raw-SI inverse-square denominators, unnormalised likelihood products, importance weights. takum reaches ±255 binades at both widths compared and never leaves range where TNF does, so the format that wins inside the window is the one that has to be selected into it. One task outcome rather than a round-trip error is also reported: on a maximum-a-posteriori estimate in raw SI units with a fixed float32 accumulator, TNF32 lands 1.60× closer to the float64 solution than takum32 and settles in 21 iterations against 27 — while binary32 beats both by a factor of thirty-three.

At matched physical width the comparison is negative. Computed from the committed reference implementations, posit holds more representable values than TNF and a finer step at unity at every width the ladder occupies — 12× finer at 19 bits, 4× at 10, 2× at 6 — and posit with es = 2 weakly dominates on both coordinates at all three. A ternary exponent does not tile a binary field: four trits use 81 of 128 exponent codes, leaving 192,512 of the 219 codes outside the format. The no-survivors corollary is accordingly withdrawn to a matched-name claim. The case for this format was never precision per bit; it is multiplier removal and decode cost. The claim that TNF4 trains where nothing else does is withdrawn: its grid had been built from codes that are not TNF words, and on the grid the format has TNF4 trains 8 of 25 MNIST runs, against 12 for fp6 e3m2 and 5 for e2m3.

A closing section sets out the ways a format comparison fails while each of its measurements is correct, since every quantitative claim above depends on those failures having been ruled out.
